steps: P1: Add a new requirement 'Reserve price': optional reserve when listing, must be at least the starting price (else rejected); auction ending with highest bid below reserve is unsold with no winner; bidders see only whether the reserve is met, never its amount. Add acceptance criteria for each rule.
P1: Amend REQ-001 to mention the optional reserve price, and REQ-004 so the highest bidder wins only if the reserve (when set) is met, otherwise the item is unsold.

P2: Item (DSN-015) gets reservePrice (number | null) and a reserveMet() method; ItemView (DSN-017) gets a reserveMet flag (boolean | null) and must not carry the reserve amount; list views of open items must also hide it.
P2: ItemController.listItem and ItemService.listItem take an optional reservePrice and validate it against the starting price; update UC-002 and SEQ-002.
P2: ItemService.closeDueAuctions marks the item unsold with no winner when the reserve is not met; update UC-005 and SEQ-005. ItemStore (DSN-029) persists the reserve column.

P2: BidEventPublisher and AuctionEventPublisher payloads carry reserveMet, never the reserve amount; WebClient (DSN-042) shows a reserve field in the listing form and 'reserve met / not met' on the item page; reflect in UC-003.

P4: Implement the changes in Item, ItemView, ItemController, ItemService, ItemStore (schema column), both publishers, the routes in app.ts (strip the reserve amount from GET /api/items and GET /api/items/:id) and public/index.html.

P5: Add tests: reserve below starting price rejected; listing without reserve still works; close below reserve gives unsold without winner; close at or above reserve gives winner; item views and live events expose reserveMet but no reserve amount; ItemStore round-trips the reserve.

text:
I saved the plan for TCK-001. It starts at **P1 (requirements)** because the ticket adds a new rule and changes two existing ones. The plan has no open questions.

**Requirements (P1)**
- A new requirement, "Reserve price":
  - A seller can set an optional reserve when listing an item. A reserve below the starting price is rejected.
  - If the highest bid at close is below the reserve, the item is unsold and has no winner.
  - Bidders only see whether the reserve is met, never the amount.
- REQ-001 (listing an item) will mention the optional reserve.
- REQ-004 (closing an auction) currently always makes the highest bidder the winner. It will be changed so that a reserve that isn't met gives an unsold item with no winner.

**Design and code that change**
- **Item and item view (DSN-015, DSN-017):** the item stores a reserve price. Clients get only a "reserve met" flag.
- **Listing an item (DSN-019, DSN-022, UC-002, SEQ-002):** takes and checks the optional reserve.
- **Closing an auction (UC-005, SEQ-005):** closing checks the reserve before naming a winner.
- **Item store (DSN-029):** saves the reserve as a new database column.
- **Live events (DSN-030, DSN-031, UC-003):** the bid and close events carry "reserve met" but not the amount.
- **Web page (DSN-042):** the listing form gets a reserve field, and the item page shows whether the reserve is met.

**Why the routes are in the plan:** today `app.ts` returns the whole stored item from `GET /api/items` and `GET /api/items/:id`. Once the item holds a reserve, those routes would show its amount to bidders, so the plan has them leave it out.

**Tests:** new tests in the UC-002, UC-003, UC-005 and DSN-029 test files. They cover the reserve check, closing below and above the reserve, that no response or event exposes the amount, and that the store saves and reads the reserve back.

The code currently matches the design (no drift), so nothing else needs fixing first.
